items.q: Why is a bank balance that never moves still a loss?
items.a: Inflation. A 1985 dollar buys what about $2.80 buys now. Cash that sits still is dying. That is the open of the 2026 beginner tape.
Billy. $200 a month from 20 to 30, then stop, ends near $813k. Jack's $300 a month from 30 to 60 ends near $678k. Billy put in about $84k less. Time, not the deposit size.

items.q: What is the one line he wants you to keep?
items.a: Don't hunt one great company. Buy all of them in one click. An ETF is that basket, trading like a stock, including a $10 slice of a $700 share.

items.q: Why isn't the S&P 500 five hundred equal bets?
items.a: [[cap-weight-index-bet]]. Bigger company, bigger slice. Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia dominate. Japan in 1989 was the sure winner, then decades of nowhere. His one-fund outs: VWRP, VT, ACWI.

sections.title: When you are allowed to sell

items.q: What are the only three good reasons to sell?
items.a: [[three-reasons-to-sell]]. Momentum died (AMC, GameStop). A clearly better use for the cash. The reason you bought is gone (Buffett dumped airlines in COVID). A red day is not on the list.

items.q: Why is a fat dividend yield not a gift?
items.a: [[dividend-total-return]]. The cash left the company. A 10% yield on a falling price can lose to a 3% yield on a growing one. Look at the payout ratio and the price, not the yield alone.
